purpose: Dipyridamole is used to help prevent blood clots from forming, especially in people who have had heart valve replacement surgery. It is also combined with aspirin (as Aggrenox) to help prevent strokes in people who have already had a stroke or a mini-stroke (TIA). Keeping your blood from clotting too easily helps protect your heart and brain.
how_it_works: Your blood contains tiny cells called platelets that clump together to form clots. Dipyridamole works by stopping these platelets from sticking together too easily. It also helps widen your blood vessels, which improves blood flow and lowers the chance of a dangerous clot forming.
common_side_effects: Headache (often the most common complaint), dizziness, upset stomach, nausea, diarrhea, flushing or feeling warm, and low blood pressure. These effects are usually mild and may improve as your body gets used to the medicine.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have low blood pressure, chest pain (angina), or myasthenia gravis before taking this medicine. Avoid caffeine (coffee, tea, energy drinks) as it can reduce how well the medicine works. Because it thins your blood, you may bleed or bruise more easily — let all your doctors and your dentist know you are taking it before any procedure or surgery. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: The usual dose for preventing clots after heart valve surgery is 75 to 100 mg taken four times a day by mouth. When combined with aspirin in the Aggrenox capsule, the typical dose is one capsule twice a day (morning and evening). Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribed and try to take it at the same times each day.
